how_steps.1: The converter identifies word boundaries (spaces, underscores, etc.).
how_steps.2: It lowercases the first word completely.
how_steps.3: It capitalizes the first letter of all subsequent words.
how_steps.4: The result is combined into a single string with no spaces.
how_steps.5: Use the converted camelCase text in your code, variable names, or API endpoints for consistent naming conventions.

faq.a1: camelCase is the practice of writing phrases without spaces, where the first letter of each word is capitalized except for the very first word.
faq.q2: Is camelCase the same as PascalCase?
faq.a2: No. PascalCase capitalizes the very first word (MyClass), while camelCase does not (myVariable).
faq.a3: The capital letters resemble the humps on a camel's back.
faq.q4: Can I use it for file names?
faq.a4: Yes, although kebab-case or snake_case are often preferred for URL-safe filenames.
faq.a5: Yes, it removes non-alphanumeric characters and use them as word boundaries.
